encoding: little-endian signed16-bit integer per normalized word
recommendation: A future bundle can store all94 arrays plus exact keys/order, lengths and per-array hashes, source raw hashes and manuscript inputs. The10short arrays add little and preserve unchanged source corpus totals and selection metadata. The original scanner consumes these exact int16 arrays; only the corpus loader would need an explicitly declared adapter.
equivalence: Every array hash was recomputed from the unchanged source normalization and agrees with the pre-target manifest. A loader adapter must validate the entire name/order/hash set, then return identical arrays and metadata; independent full array equality and same-source small fixture output parity should precede any new bundle claim.
limits: This assessment only computes sizes in memory. No derived arrays or corpus bytes are saved, distributed, or used for a new scan. Word-length arrays omit word spellings, but no legal conclusion about redistribution is asserted. An array bundle reuses recorded normalization; it does not independently rerun normalization or authenticate historical224-text bytes.
